habitat: Throughout moist and dry deciduous forests, plains, and foothills
ecological_importance: Nectar source for bees, butterflies, and various insect pollinators; dense canopy provides nesting sites and roosting cover for avifauna.
field_identification_notes: Whorled leaves (typically 6-7 leaves radiating from a single node).
Abundant bitter white latex exuded from broken petioles or bark.
Rough, corky, deeply fissured grayish bark.
Slender, dangling, bean-like paired follicles in mature trees.
Strong, sweet-heavy fragrance during flowering season (October-December).
ml_relevance: Whorled leaf arrangement at nodes is the single most diagnostic computer vision feature for distinguishing A. scholaris from other avenue trees.

ar_information.quick_identification: Whorled leaves in clusters of 6-7; milky latex; rough corky bark; slender hanging pods.
ar_information.ecological_importance: Nectar-rich flowers support diverse insect pollinators; dense shade provider.
ar_information.conservation_message: Least Concern (LC). The specific epithet scholaris refers to its historical use in manufacturing wooden writing slates for school children.
